title: An interior-point algorithm for large-scale nonlinear optimization with inexact step computations
contribution: A matrix-free line-search interior-point method that extends the SMART termination tests of the equality-constrained inexact Newton line to inequality constraints via slack scaling, proves global convergence (including to infeasible stationary points), and shows within Ipopt/PARDISO that iterative solves beat direct factorization in CPU time on 3-D PDE-constrained problems.
problem_entry: Problems with millions of variables where factorization is intractable; nonlinear elimination and reduced-space PDE methods each have named drawbacks (repeated accurate solves, bounds becoming nonlinear, no state constraints) (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Scale slacks so the barrier-subproblem primal-dual system matches the predecessor [16]; normal/tangential split with a trust region of radius omega*||A^T c||; three SMART tests on penalty-model reduction; inertia-free Hessian modification; slack reset; Armijo on the computable model reduction (pp. 4-11).
assumptions: C1 functions; Assumption 3.1 (finite modifications reach W >= 2 theta I, solver reaches arbitrary accuracy) and 3.3 (bounded Lipschitz derivatives, bounded W) (pp. 12-13); LICQ only for multipliers (p. 19); flexible-penalty swap claimed not to affect theory (p. 20).
proof_devices: Proof by reference: method 'intentionally constructed to resemble' [16], only line-search lemmas re-proved (pp. 11-12)
Log-barrier one-variable bound giving a model-accuracy inequality with xi1*pi*alpha^2||d||^2 (Lemma 3.5, p. 13)
Scaled and shifted penalty phi-hat = (phi - chi)/pi + ||c|| monotone despite pi increases; slack boundedness via (ln s)/s -> 0 (Lemma 3.6, p. 14)
Contradiction on the set Xi = {||A^T c|| >= xi}: test-2-only iterations cannot persist, uniform step bound, constant decrease (Lemma 3.9, pp. 15-16)
Outer-loop trichotomy theorem: infeasible stationary / pi -> infinity / feasible KKT under LICQ (Theorem 3.13, pp. 18-19)
experiments: Inside Ipopt 3.7.0 with PARDISO SQMR + multilevel ILU vs default Ipopt with PARDISO direct; 684 CUTEr/COPS problems (pre-run exclusions: two-sided constraints, n <= p), full exit-status table, success 85% vs 94%, objectives agree except 8 vs 23 cases; 3-D PDE boundary control up to n = 512,000 (3,402 s vs 33,704 s at N = 50) and hyperthermia up to n = 125,020 (pp. 19-26).
positioning: Continues Byrd-Curtis-Nocedal 2008/2010 and Curtis-Nocedal-Waechter 2009 as an explicit ladder (p. 2); contrasts with full-space PDE methods (no inequalities, weaker guarantees) and reduced-space methods (projection cost, no state bounds) (p. 3); Waechter-Biegler failure example motivates the normal-step trust region (pp. 5, 27).
writing: Goal sentence then one-sentence contribution (p. 2); exact-step framework (Alg. 2.1) before the inexact algorithm (Alg. 2.2) (pp. 7, 10-11); hedged results ('preliminary', 'very encouraging') and owned failures ('Our approach fails more often', p. 24); roadmap promises future work that the conclusion barely gives (pp. 3, 26-27).
limits_future: Only an algebraic sparsity-based preconditioner; problem-specific preconditioning deferred (p. 3); code less mature than Ipopt and slower on some small problems (p. 24); two-sided constraints unsupported (p. 23); no local rate analysis.

method_links.note: SMART tests derived from penalty-model reduction; primal residual not controlled explicitly; tests must be enforced in the scaled system; Hessian modification triggered by the tests not inertia
Rival is the same Ipopt code with only the linear solver switched (direct vs iterative PARDISO); incumbent's higher success rate and better objectives printed
One algorithm with convergence to infeasible stationary points; flexible penalty adopted because a large early pi hampered progress

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Inequality extension built so the scaled system is the one in [16]; analysis proved by citation, only the line-search parts re-proved

transferable: Rescale variables so an extended Newton system is formally the predecessor's; reuse its tests and lemmas and re-prove only what the new terms touch (pp. 5, 11-12)
Normal-step trust region with radius omega*||A^T c||: vanishes at infeasible stationary points, no radius-update heuristic (p. 5)
Armijo condition on the computable model reduction instead of the directional derivative (p. 10)
Slack reset s <- max{s, c_I(x)} so ||A^T c|| -> 0 certifies stationarity of the infeasibility measure (pp. 7, 18)
Prove monotonicity of phi-hat = (phi - chi)/pi + ||c|| when the penalty parameter can grow (pp. 14-15)
Compare against the incumbent inside the same production code and linear-algebra package, reporting full exit-status tables (pp. 19, 23)
Aim for a tighter residual bound first, fall back to the bare termination tests after a fixed number of Krylov iterations (p. 22)

quotes.text: Our approach fails more often, but this is to be expected, as our code is not as mature as IPOPT and an increase in iteration count often follows from the use of inexact Newton steps.
the benefits of these techniques are only realized if inexact step computations are allowed and controlled appropriately in order to guarantee global convergence of the algorithm.

title: An inexact Newton method for nonconvex equality constrained optimization
contribution: Extends the SMART-test inexact SQP method to nonconvex equality-constrained problems by judging steps only through a sufficient reduction in an exact-penalty model, with an inertia-free rule for when to perturb the Hessian, and proves global convergence without convexity of the primal-dual systems.
problem_entry: The 2008 inexact SQP needs strict convexity; convexifying requires inertia, which matrix-free methods lack; full-space nonconvex inexact methods are an empty cell between factorizing full-space and inexact reduced-space methods (pp. 2, 4).
key_idea: Forgo the QP interpretation of the step and accept it by its effect on the penalty model: Delta m >= max{1/2 d'Wd, theta*Upsilon} + sigma*pi*max{||c||, ||r||-||c||}; Test I (old pi) and Test II (constraint reduction, licenses a pi increase); modify W only when neither can pass (pp. 4-11).
assumptions: Smooth f, c; bounded functions and derivatives, bounded multipliers, full-row-rank Jacobians with singular values bounded below, bounded W, consistent primal-dual systems (Assumption 1, p. 12); positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian dropped (p. 13).
proof_devices: Normal-component bound via the pseudo-inverse A^T(AA^T)^-1 and residual bounds (Lemma 1, pp. 13-14)
Directional derivative bounded by -gamma4(Upsilon + max{||c||, ||r||}) (Lemma 3, p. 14)
Bounded penalty parameter by a three-case split on curvature and the ratio ||u||^2 / ||v||^2, each giving a loss O(||c|| - ||r||) (Lemma 4, pp. 15-16)
Step-length lower bound from a Taylor bound with a finite pi-hat (Lemma 5, p. 17)
Telescoping merit decrease giving ||c_k|| -> 0, d_k -> 0, then the final theorem by citing Theorem 4.10 of the predecessor (Lemma 6 and Theorem 5.1, pp. 17-18)
experiments: Matlab, unpreconditioned GMRES (MINRES/SQMR similar), 44 CUTEr problems after filters n+t <= 1000 and a run-based Assumption-1 filter (any Jacobian singular value < 1e-4 encountered); mechanism log of % Test I/II and positive-eigenvalue counts; rivals ISQP-naive (fails 8) and factorizing ISQP-ideal; explicit failure definitions; performance profiles on outer and inner iterations (pp. 18-25).
positioning: Builds directly on Byrd-Curtis-Nocedal 2008; credits inexact reduced-space SQP (Heinkenschloss-Vicente, Ulbrich, Heinkenschloss-Ridzal) and nonconvex factorizing methods; insists it is not a penalty method per se; claims no inertia-free line-search competitor exists (pp. 4-5, 22).
writing: Central condition built in Sect. 3 from the unconstrained exact case to the inexact constrained case, called 'the centerpiece' (pp. 6-9); each test followed by the kind of step it admits (pp. 10-11); mild affect ('comforting', 'surprisingly robust'); final remarks give practical extensions not open problems (pp. 20-26).
limits_future: Equality constraints only; full-rank Jacobians; no preconditioner; problems with n+t <= 1000; large-scale study outside scope; inexactness parameters to be tuned per application (pp. 12, 18, 20); future: apply to barrier subproblems of an interior-point method (p. 25).

method_links.note: Sufficient merit-model reduction decides acceptance, Hessian perturbation and penalty change during the iterative solve; inertia-free Hessian Modification Strategy; factorizing ISQP-ideal as ceiling
Rivals are one-switch variants of the same framework: naive (drop curvature safeguard) and ideal (add inertia information)
No outside rival (none claimed to exist); text silent on problems where INS needs far more inner iterations than both rivals (eigenc2 57,714 vs 8,687 / 3,625)

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Method automatically reduces to the 2008 inexact SQP in convex regions; final theorem obtained by matching the predecessor's limits

transferable: Acceptance rule max{1/2 d'Wd, theta||d||^2}: keeps the convex-case step yet guarantees sufficient descent under negative curvature (p. 7)
Derive the acceptance condition in staged displays: exact unconstrained, constrained convex, failure case, inexact (pp. 6-9)
Computable bounds nu = ||Ad||^2/||A||^2 <= ||v||^2 and Upsilon = ||d||^2 - ||Ad||^2/||A||^2 >= ||u||^2 for unobservable step components (pp. 19-20)
Scale-invariant curvature threshold theta = 1e-8 max{||W||_1, 1} (p. 18)
Bracket a new method between a naive floor (drop the safeguard) and an idealized ceiling (use the unavailable information) built in the same code (pp. 22-24)
Log per-problem % of steps accepted by each termination test and eigenvalue counts after modification (pp. 21-22)
Prove penalty-parameter boundedness by showing every increase occurs only where the objective-model loss is O(||c|| - ||r||) (pp. 15-16)

quotes.text: we intend to forgo the interpretation of our step as an (approximate) solution to a local optimization subproblem and instead jump straight to its effect on our globalization mechanism.
The resulting algorithm fully integrates the procedures of step computation and step selection and automatically reduces to an inexact SQP method in convex regions of the search space.

title: A sequential quadratic programming algorithm for nonconvex, nonsmooth constrained optimization
contribution: SQP-GS: an l1-penalty SQP method whose QP uses independently sampled gradients of objective and each constraint, proved globally convergent with probability one to stationary points of the penalty function or of the constraint violation, with a public Matlab code and an ablation showing sampling is essential.
problem_entry: Locally Lipschitz, a.e.-differentiable nonconvex objective and constraints with solutions at kinks; join smooth SQP and unconstrained gradient sampling, arguing that plain SQP is steepest-descent-like and fails on nonsmooth problems (pp. 1-4).
key_idea: Insert gradients sampled in an epsilon-ball into the linearizations of an l1-penalty SQP QP, linearized at f(x_k), c_j(x_k); independent sample sets per function; decrease rho only when the model reduction is small and violation exceeds theta; shrink epsilon on small model reduction (pp. 3-8).
assumptions: Locally Lipschitz, C1 on open dense sets (Assumption 3.1, p. 9); bounded iterates/samples and uniformly bounded positive definite H_k (Assumption 3.2, p. 9); calmness for exact penalization (Theorems 2.1-2.2, p. 5); p >= n+1 samples; iterates kept in D for analysis (p. 8).
proof_devices: Model reduction equals 1/2 d'Hd, so a small reduction certifies epsilon-stationarity (Lemma 3.6, p. 10)
Descent of the penalty via the directional-derivative formula over active and violated linearized constraints (Lemma 3.7, p. 11)

Caratheodory points plus small balls give a positive-probability set T of good sample sets; persistent bad iterations are a probability-zero event (Lemma 3.8 and Theorem 3.3 cases 1a/1b, pp. 12-13, 15)
QP solution bounded via the minimum-norm minimizer of the violation model (Lemma 3.9, pp. 13-14)
Kiwiel's gradient-sampling convergence proof extended to the case rho -> 0 (pp. 14-16)
experiments: Matlab with MOSEK; L-BFGS H_k with safeguards; no sampling for known-smooth functions (conjecture); parameters chosen during the experiments; 10 random starting points, 500 iterations, termination off; nonsmooth Rosenbrock with kink solution, eigenvalue-product, l_q compressed sensing (q = 1, 0.5; exact and noisy), robust quadratic constraint; p = 0 ablation fails on all problems; no external rival; best-run reporting for Examples 5.2-5.3 (pp. 16-24).
positioning: Generalizes S1QP (p = 0) and gradient sampling (m = 0); distinguishes itself from bundle cutting planes on linearization point and fresh sampling; closest to bundle(-filter) methods but differs in detail; reformulation and penalty approaches listed without critique (pp. 3-4, 9).
writing: Contribution framed as generalization of two parents (p. 9); necessity of GS argued then demonstrated (pp. 4, 19-20); rejected simplifications given explicit reasons (p. 7); modest framing ('preliminary implementation', special-purpose solvers likely better, p. 19); concrete tailoring ideas in the conclusion (pp. 24-25).
limits_future: Fresh gradient samples every iteration may be prohibitive; QP with p(m+1) cuts is the main cost; no rate analysis; future: tailored/null-space sampling, smaller QP for convex problems, SLP-GS (cheaper per iteration but much slower rate, unproven) (pp. 3, 18, 25).

method_links.note: p = 0 ablation switching off only gradient sampling, poor on every test problem
No tuned external rival (only 'comparable to' [8]); parameters decided during the experiments; best-of-10 reporting for Examples 5.2-5.3
Single algorithm with an infeasible-stationarity outcome (rho -> 0), but rho is decreased by a fixed factor at epsilon-stationarity events, not by a progress-based steering rule inside the step
Success judged by a KKT-based error estimate tracked as best per sampling radius, with the solver's own termination turned off

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: With p = 0 the method is S1QP and with m = 0 a gradient-sampling method
Independent sample sets per function are required by Lemma 3.8; their generation cost is argued insignificant next to gradient evaluations and the QP

transferable: Linearize sampled gradients at the current function value (f(x_k) + grad f(x)'d), not at the sample point, so the model works without convexity (p. 3)
One computable quantity (model reduction) drives the line search, the sampling-radius decrease and the penalty/tolerance updates (pp. 7-8)
Ablate exactly the new component (p = 0) on every problem and show trajectories from the same starting points side by side (pp. 19-20)
Probability-one convergence: build an explicit positive-measure set of good samples near any non-stationary limit via Caratheodory (pp. 12-13)
Track the best optimality estimate per sampling radius because single estimates depend on the sample set (p. 17)
Write the reason each tempting simplification is rejected: lost scale invariance, discarded information, or the proof step it breaks (p. 7)

quotes.text: We emphasize that the GS procedure in our approach is necessary for ensuring theoretical convergence guarantees since a basic SQP strategy (without GS) will fail in theory and in practice.
The remaining values were decided upon during the course of our experiments.
